Add the no-worker-identifiers rule and its email check (#292)

Add the adopter-owned rule under .claude/rules/external/ that bars any
worker email address, account identifier, seat label, or other
third-party identifier from every public or potentially public
surface, and link it from the Adopted governance section of
.claude/CLAUDE.md.

Add tools/test-no-worker-identifiers.py, which reads the raw bytes of
every regular file that git ls-files lists (a tracked symbolic link
and a submodule are not read) and the name of every path it lists,
and takes every candidate address around every at sign, so an exempt
candidate cannot hide another, with work that grows linearly with the
file. 2 exemptions, each tested on a candidate folded to lower case,
so each holds in any letter case: (1) the candidate is exactly the
maintainer's own email address; (2) the domain of the candidate is
reserved for documentation: its last label is invalid, test, or
example, or it is, or ends with a dot and then, example.com,
example.org, or example.net. An at sign passes only when every
candidate that the scan reads at it is exempt, under either
exemption, so an address passes only when each shorter domain that it
holds, ending after 2 or more letters that follow a dot, gives an
exempt candidate as well. 1 exact-line allowlist entry covers the
URL-userinfo fixture in tools/test-release-links.py; a stale entry
fails. A failure names the file, the line number, and a digest of the
match, never its text, and names a path whose name holds a match only
by a digest of the path name; a red run prints every failure in full.
A failed git call, a git that cannot start, an empty listing, a
missing file, or an unreadable file fails closed. Each caught example
in the suite is assembled at run time, so its source holds no
matchable text.

Run the suite as a named step of the Orchestration registry workflow,
name it in the header of that workflow, mirror it in
tools/run_all_checks.sh, and record the new sha256 of that script in
tools/test-run-all-checks.py, which pins it.

Residual: the check covers the email class only. Seat labels, bare
handles, and numeric account identifiers rest on the rule itself, and
a surface that is not a file, such as a pull request description, is
not reached. The full residual list, with each form that passes and
each place that is not read, is in the rule,
.claude/rules/external/no-worker-identifiers.md.
